steps_json.detail_en: Measure CO2 near the breathing zone with the handheld capnograph. Values above 3.5 mmHg point to stagnant air pockets in weightlessness.
Move the crew member to the main Habitat A air duct and set the fan speed to 100%. If dizziness occurs or CO2 exceeds 4.5 mmHg, give mask oxygen at 4 L/min.
Drink 400 mL of water with electrolytes. If the headache persists after 30 minutes in clean air (below 2.8 mmHg), use the approved relief items in Drawer B2.

escalation_en: Blurred vision, confusion, shortness of breath at rest, or cabin CO2 above 5.0 mmHg.
source_en: Habitable Atmosphere technical brief; Natural and Induced Environments Vol. 2 (cabin air quality).

title_en: Neuro-Ocular Sheath Elevation & Visual Shift Management

steps_json.detail_en: Repeat bilateral optic nerve sheath ultrasound measurement with 3.0 mm axial guide.
Record intraocular pressure and visual acuity chart score for both eyes.
Schedule lower-body negative pressure countermeasure session per protocol.
Queue bilateral ocular telemetry bundle for flight surgeon review.

escalation_en: Escalate to onboard physician if either optic sheath exceeds 5.5 mm or acute visual distortion occurs.
source_en: Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome clinical brief (exams at pre-flight, day 30, day 90, 30 days before return and post-flight).

steps_json.detail_en: Verify quiet hours enforcement (22:00-06:00 UTC) and cabin lighting spectrum.
Reduce non-essential EVA workload for 24 hours if sleep efficiency drops below 78%.
Run 2-minute cognitive reaction baseline prior to pilot duty rotation.

escalation_en: Escalate to onboard physician if deep sleep stays below 45 minutes for 3 consecutive nights.
source_en: NCBI Bookshelf NBK526132 Physiology, Sleep Stages; National Sleep Foundation - What is Sleep Quality.

steps_json.detail_en: Confirm cabin ambient noise is below 55 dBA before acoustic capture.
Record 30-second cardiac auscultation across mitral and aortic sites.
Administer electrolyte hydration pack and monitor recovery heart rate for 10 minutes.

escalation_en: Escalate to onboard physician if resting heart rate remains above 110 bpm or abnormal murmur persists.
source_en: MedlinePlus - Pulse; Reduced Cardiorespiratory and Musculoskeletal Fitness risk report.

steps_json.detail_en: Drink 400 mL of water with electrolytes, then spread the rest of the daily goal (30-35 mL per kg of body mass) across the shift.
Compare with the color strip in Pouch B2-11: levels 1-3 are well hydrated, 4-6 need more fluid, 7 or darker means dehydration.
Log every drink and repeat the color check. Avoid hard exercise until the color returns to level 3 or lighter.

escalation_en: Urine color at level 7 or darker after drinking, dizziness when standing, confusion or no urine for 8 hours.
source_en: HPRC - How to assess hydration status using urine color charts; GSSI - Urine markers for hydration monitoring.

steps_json.detail_en: Gather the crew in the storm shelter with the water-wall shielding until the daily dose falls back under 0.6 mSv.
Reschedule any spacewalk and keep the personal dosimeter on during the whole shift.
Record the dose for each crew member. The yearly working limit is 20 mSv; Earth background is 2.4-3.0 mSv per year.

escalation_en: Nausea, vomiting or skin redness after exposure, or a daily dose above 10 mSv.
source_en: Radiation Protection technical brief; The Human Body in Space.

steps_json.detail_en: Stop the task and secure the crew member and loose objects nearby. Ask what happened, where it hurts and whether they blacked out.
Check that they know their name, the date and where they are. Look for swelling, a bent shape or pain when moving the limb.
Hold a cold pack wrapped in cloth on the area for 15 minutes. Keep a painful limb still with the splint from the drawer.
Repeat the name, date and place check every 15 minutes for 2 hours.

escalation_en: Call the crew physician now if they blacked out, vomit, are confused, have a severe headache, cannot move the limb or the limb looks bent.
source_en: World Health Organization. Basic Emergency Care: approach to the acutely ill and injured (2018).

steps_json.detail_en: Put on gloves from the drawer. Press a clean gauze pad firmly on the cut for 10 minutes without lifting it. If blood soaks through, add more gauze on top and keep pressing.
Catch floating droplets with absorbent wipes and seal them in a bag.
Once bleeding stops, rinse the cut with clean water. Close small cuts with adhesive strips and cover with a dry dressing.
Check the dressing and the skin around it twice a day for redness or warmth.

escalation_en: Call the crew physician now if bleeding does not stop after 10 minutes of firm pressure, the cut is deep or gaping, or there is numbness beyond the wound.
source_en: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies. International First Aid, Resuscitation and Education Guidelines (2020).

title_en: Taking Medicine Safely and Side Effects

steps_json.detail_en: Read the name, dose and expiry date before taking it. Confirm with the crew physician before starting any new medicine.
Log the medicine, dose and time in the health log right away. Do not take two medicines with the same active ingredient at once.
Avoid sleep aids within 8 hours of a piloting or repair shift.
Watch for rash, itching, dizziness, stomach upset or unusual sleepiness. If one appears, stop the medicine and log what you feel.

escalation_en: Call the crew physician now if there is swelling of the face or throat, trouble breathing, a spreading rash or fainting after taking a medicine.
source_en: World Health Organization. Model List of Essential Medicines, 23rd list (2023).
